#35708. ‘The Hairiest 90 Minutes of My Career’: How the FAA Ground Stop Went Down

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1184 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

‘The Hairiest 90 Minutes of My Career’: How the FAA Ground Stop Went Down

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, by Wednesday of this week—six days after a 4.5-hour nationwide ground stop that panicked onlookers and scrambled air travel—US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said he still wasn’t quite sure what led to the Friday meltdown.
  • Still, the Federal Aviation Administration has revealed that a few things did go wrong on Friday afternoon.
  • The agency has since described the ground stop as something executed “out of an abundance of caution.” On Wednesday, FAA administrator Bryan Bedford appeared to downplay the incident even as he took blame for it, calling the outage “a knee scrape, and I’m sorry.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, by Wednesday of this week—six days after a 4.5-hour nationwide ground stop that panicked onlookers and scrambled air travel—US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said he still wasn’t quite sure what led to the Friday meltdown. “The root cause of what happened, we don’t have clarity yet,” he said after a meeting with lawmakers.

Still, the Federal Aviation Administration has revealed that a few things did go wrong on Friday afternoon. It involved routine infrastructure replacement, a faulty router, data overload, and disruption in some regions in the radio communications that air traffic controllers use to speak to each other and pilots.

The agency has since described the ground stop as something executed “out of an abundance of caution.” On Wednesday, FAA administrator Bryan Bedford appeared to downplay the incident even as he took blame for it, calling the outage “a knee scrape, and I’m sorry.”.

While aviation industry workers maintain that flyers were safe throughout the ground stop, some felt government officials downplayed the event, which left air traffic controllers scrambling to backup frequencies even as they tried to figure out what was going on.

“That was the hairiest 90 minutes of my career,” one air traffic controller told WIRED.

Contacted for comment, FAA spokesperson Steve Kulm didn't answer questions but referred WIRED to the agency’s ground stop Q&A web page, where the agency writes it has “clear, established, standard procedures to ensure safety during incidents such as this.” It states that some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained online during the communication challenges, “allowing air traffic controllers to maintain communication with and track aircraft.”.

Here’s what we know about the ground stop so far.

To understand the communications issues that led to the ground stop, here’s a quick overview on how air traffic control works.

Most flyers are familiar with the towers near airports, officially called the Airport Traffic Control Towers (ATCT). The controllers who work here manage aircraft ground movements, including takeoffs and landings. Once an aircraft gets up into the sky, around 10,000 feet, it’s passed to controllers in a Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) center, who manage airport arrivals and departures. Then, once a flight is really underway, an aircraft is passed to Air Route Traffic Control Centers, often just called Centers. There are 22 of these in the US, and controllers there guide airplanes for most of their flight, passing off the aircraft as they move between regions.

The communication radios used at Centers have a range of around 150 miles—a problem when the areas they have to manage are more than 100,000 square miles each. So phone lines at the Centers lead to networks of transmitters, each installed remotely.

According to recent reports, for decades, this network has been connected by copper telecommunications lines—outdated and sometimes brittle tech. So in 2025’s GOP-led Big Beautiful Bill, the Transportation Department received the billions of dollars in funding needed to upgrade that copper to fiber-optic cables. The upgrade swaps the system, the private communications backbone of Air Traffic Control, from one of mechanical switches to a digital system built on internet-based protocols. A contractor called L3Harris—the network owner—manages the transition, and as of last week, the project was about 70 percent complete. This was where the FAA ran into problems.

The trouble began in El Dorado, Arkansas, the site of one of those remote communications facilities, which is part of the larger Center based in Memphis, Tennessee. There, the FAA indicates a contractor with L3Harris was making on Friday what is now a routine switch from that legacy copper system to a fiber-optic one. But something, it appears, went wrong when the worker plugged in a latest router as part of that transition, and the FAA still doesn’t know why.

Data began to flood the network, making 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds, according to the FAA. The agency claims another remote site, a radar-based facility in Amarillo, Texas, may have also flooded the network with data. To compensate, the network tried to recruit other nodes, and they got overloaded, too, taking down several radio frequencies on the network.

Recent findings suggest that at first, the concern manifested as intermittent dropouts on radio frequencies at Centers in the region, from Kansas City to Chicago, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke to WIRED under the condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak to the press. This made it difficult, if not impossible, for air traffic controllers to talk between Centers and with pilots through normal channels. From there, though, the issues seem to have cascaded to other regions, including the areas around Washington, DC, and New York.

In control rooms—mostly Centers dealing with en route flights—air traffic controllers first noticed some “dropouts” on their radio transmissions, according to two sources. On their own, these sorts of communication disruptions aren’t unheard of. But when they began to spread to multiple regions, FAA officials really began to pay attention.

Because officials didn’t understand why the radio frequencies were unstable, the agency called a nationwide ground stop.

In a recent development, one person who spoke with WIRED noted they still had access to a backup frequency during the network instability. The FAA said “some frequencies and radar feeds remained reliable.”.

According to recent reports, then, according to the FAA, contractors from L3 Harris blocked data from the remote Arkansas and Texas locations from the wider network. That restabilized the system, restoring radio contact between everyone in the airspace.

In a statement Friday, a spokesperson for the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, a union that represents almost 20,000 controllers, wrote that “air traffic controllers were on the job, carrying out their responsibilities and working to ensure the safety of the National Airspace System.”.

It has been revealed that while the technical complications led to several uncomfortable hours for aviation professionals, midair passengers remained safe during the ground stop, claims Scott Miller, an airline pilot and a lecturer in the Aviation and Technology program at San Jose State University in California. “It was certainly an abnormal situation, but it wasn’t an emergency, because we’ve trained for it,” he says. “It was not dangerous, but it was highly inconveniencing, and it was not normal.”.

According to recent reports, it helped that the radio outage did not seem to have affected all Centers, and even fewer TRACONs and local towers. That means pilots were generally in contact with controllers, especially as they circled airports and landed their planes.

It also helped that pilots don’t actually need air traffic control to fly their planes, Miller claims. “Talking to a controller is not what keeps an airplane in the sky,” he says. Pilots have plenty of systems onboard that allow them to “see” what’s going on around them.

Despite the lack of clarity on what exactly happened with the newly installed router to make it malfunction, Duffy has settled on a solution: more money. On Wednesday, he officially asked Congress for $50 billion, with $30 billion of that dedicated to air traffic control modernization.

#35707. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2340 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover.
  • This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
  • Sources indicate that the reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.

This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.

Sources indicate that the reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.

But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.

Sources indicate that taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.

According to recent reports, A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.

It has been revealed that of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.

Recent findings suggest that lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some notable depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.

While Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).

There’s a minor relationship simulation component to the game, with a simple “heart level” that can rise or fall based on some basic decisions. Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.

In true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.

In a recent development, for the first half of the game, the pair are constantly interacting with a rogues’ gallery of fresh criminal acquaintances, each more over-the-top than the last, and all of them having specific needs that somehow only Jason and Lucia can fulfill. Many of the missions these small-time crooks have on offer end up feeling like the criminal equivalent of errands—drive here, take that, lose the cops, repeat.

And while a few standout characters develop complex interpersonal relationships with Jason and Lucia over multiple missions, most of these early side characters feel like one-note caricatures that can be distilled to a few tropey traits.

It isn’t until the back half of the game that the main storyline really starts to focus on what it does best: integrating Jason and Lucia into a persistent ring of professional criminals working toward bigger and bigger scores. Here, the missions build on each other, with characters going undercover, casing targets, and learning fresh skills that eventually come together in some truly tense and bombastic heists. These missions also do the best job of showing off the dual protagonist system, frequently shifting the perspective between Jason and Lucia to highlight their different skills and views on how things are going down.

In a recent development, outside of this core plot, though, many of the missions and side stories in GTA VI make Jason and Lucia feel like side characters in their own story. I found myself beginning to tune out during some of the many missions in which one or both protagonists serve as glorified security props or overpaid getaway drivers amid other characters’ contrived turf wars. And even dozens of hours into the game, there were still missions that felt like tutorials, seemingly built around the opportunity to introduce some upcoming simulation system or control scheme.

Recent findings suggest that through it all, the game can’t seem to totally shake the style of sophomoric humor that feels a lot less “edgy” today than it did when Grand Theft Auto III hit back in 2001 (for players who are old enough to remember that release, at least). There are countless extended bits where the entire joke seems to boil down to “Man, kinky sex is weird, isn’t it?” or “Hey look, it’s a male penis (or something that looks similar to one).” And the game seems to take particular pleasure in forcing Jason into uncomfortable situations with plenty of T&A, much to Lucia’s good-natured bemusement.

A word of warning for parents: This is a game that definitely earns a hard “M for Mature” rating and reveals how standards for that rating have shifted since GTA: San Andreas earned an AO re-rating for hiding a single sex scene amid its legacy code.

There are moments where GTA VI’s satire cuts a bit deeper. I especially liked a couple of side stories that skewered buzzword-spewing crypto bros and multi-level marketing schemes with some welcome over-the-top excess. Overall, though, the game’s warmed-over one-liner takes on “wokeness” felt about as fresh as jokes about mothers-in-law and TV dinners, without much in the way of thought-provoking statements on society as a whole in 2026.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI has a gift for finding excuses to lure you into an expertly designed space and then throwing together a reason for why you have to shoot/punch your way out. That might sound snarky, but I actually mean it more or less sincerely; I was frequently surprised by the scenarios the writers dreamed up to turn what seemed like a routine trip to some beautiful locale into a firefight with way more armed goons than seems strictly necessary.

The moment-to-moment shooting will feel very familiar to Grand Theft Auto fans, by which I mean it’s dead simple to hide behind convenient cover and pop up to pick off relatively stupid enemies one by one with a dizzying array of available weaponry. The rare enemies that do manage to flank you seem to have incredibly bad aim, even at close range, and both Jason and Lucia can take a whole lot more punishment than the average quick-to-crumble grunt.

Recent findings suggest that driving around town is significantly more exciting—you’ll be darting between cars in heavy traffic to chase down antagonists, avoid the police, or simply get where you’re going faster. It’s still a blast to sample as many vehicles as you can, from zippy but easy-to-wreck sports cars to tank-like trucks that can plow through traffic, tiny motorbikes that can squeeze through tight spaces, and off-road vehicles that can explore off the beaten path.

Sources indicate that driving through the city also offers ample opportunities to get distracted from your main goals by dozens of side activities that dot the map. Even as I struggled to work through the story on deadline, I found myself getting sucked in for hours trying to master drone racing, chasing gold medals in countless mud-splattered rally races, or hunting for one of the many meditation spots hidden in out-of-the-way corners.

While most of these side activities offer money or improve character stats, some are simply there to be experienced. Completionists will have a bear of a time tracking down every single hidden collectible, rare car, robbable location, and beautiful landmark the developers have placed throughout the city. Grand Theft Auto VI seems set to be one of those games you can just load up to hang out in long after the main story missions are done.

According to recent reports, even with a fast vehicle, much of that “hang out” time can be spent simply crossing the game’s massive map. Getting from the depths of the wilderness in the north to the tip of the keys in the south is a six-plus-mile trip (measured at an apparently real-world-accurate scale) that can take 10 minutes to weave your way across on a good traffic day. During these cross-city treks, the tenor of the city’s architecture morphs noticeably as you pass from rich gated communities through the glitzy skyscraper-laden downtown and on to downtrodden neighborhoods, backwoods swamps, and laid-back island beach communities.

According to recent reports, as nice as Vice City’s outdoor architecture is, GTA VI’s interiors are where the game’s developers really show off. Practically every story mission seems to introduce a latest cavernous indoor space that’s fully furnished and lovingly crafted to look naturally lived-in and also utterly unlike anything you’ve seen before. And while you can’t go into every one of the thousands of buildings you pass on the streets of Vice City, you can enter a surprisingly large number, each with its own distinct layout and decorations.

Another element that makes all these spaces feel lived-in is the game’s surprisingly detailed crowd system. Grand Theft Auto VI sometimes packs over a hundred non-player characters into a single space, with no two characters looking or acting alike in size, shape, dress, or animation. Working your way through these crowds can be integral to some of the game’s missions, but even when you’re just casually exploring, it’s fun to take advantage of eavesdropping opportunities, listening in on individual conversations that build into overlapping chatter (realistically muffled through walls and over distance).

Grand Theft Auto VI’s spaces also seem specifically designed to show off the game’s incredible lighting system, which really shines on a PS5 Pro. The effect is most apparent at night, when car headlights streaming through a window or the rotating blue-and-red of a cop car can cast the entire world in an otherworldly glow.

But even in “normal” lighting conditions, I’d occasionally find myself slack-jawed at the details: a laptop screen partially reflected in a character’s glasses, the way rotating pyrotechnic laser effects played across dancers in a crowded club, the fluttering shadows cast by a leafy tree near sunset, or the finger smudges visible on your cell phone in bright sunshine.

I could go on and on about the little “attention to detail” touches that add up to a more engaging world simulation. Characters who fall in the dirt get dust on only the specific parts of their clothes that hit the ground. Older characters look distinctly wrinkly, with veins that show through their thinning skin. Fabric and hair flow naturally in the wind and as characters move. Rain beads on car roofs and drips off overhangs during a storm.

Through it all, one moment really stood out to me. As I prepared for an upcoming firefight, I had Lucia start eating some chips to buff her health. Halfway through the bag, I had her pick up a nearby soda, too. At first, Lucia held the chip bag in one hand and used the other to pick out individual chips. But once that other hand was occupied with a soda, she started shaking the bag above her head to pour the chips directly into her mouth.

It has been revealed that when I thought about the effort that went into coding and recording that specific animation for such a highly specific edge case, I thought about the millions of man-hours that went into making Grand Theft Auto VI the ultimate expression of this kind of urban crime/life sim. It might be a long time before we see this level of focused effort on a singular interactive vision again.

Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death.

A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani, the Department of Justice noted.

Asif Merchant, who had alleged ties to Iran, sought to hire a hitman to assassinate a politician or a government official in the United States, a Brooklyn court found.

Recent findings suggest that suleimani, the head of Iran’s foreign military operations, was killed in a US drone strike in Baghdad in January 2020. Iranian officials have repeatedly vowed to avenge his killing.

Merchant had testified that he was forced into the plot to protect his family in the Iranian capital Tehran from the Guards, adding that he thought he would get caught before anyone was killed, multiple media outlets reported.

He noted he was never ordered to kill a specific person but noted his Iranian contact had mentioned three people in connection with the plot – Trump, the former US president Joe Biden and former UN ambassador Nikki Haley.

But Todd Blanche, the United States attorney general, insisted on Tuesday that the plot was against Trump.

“An Iranian agent who came to the United States to coordinate an assassination attempt against President Trump has been justly sentenced for his criminal conduct,” Blanche remarked after Merchant was sentenced to 330 months’ imprisonment.

“The Department of Justice will not tolerate foreign terrorist plots against our leaders and will not stop until those responsible are held accountable.”.

US officials previously noted Merchant had “close ties to Iran” and described his alleged plot as “straight out of the Iranian regime’s playbook”.

Merchant was arrested on 12 July 2024 as he planned to leave the country.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Crimean Bridge was attacked for a third time this week, a Russian official said on Thursday.

Rail traffic had been temporarily suspended, according to Crimea's Russian-installed governor.

"The damage is presently being assessed," Sergei Aksyonov, the governor, initially mentioned on Telegram, adding that emergency services were at the scene.

Aksyonov later announced that traffic was set to be restored starting from around 4 p.m. local time (1300 GMT).

TASS news agency reported it may take a few months for some sections of the bridge to become operational, citing Deputy ​Prime Minister Marat ⁠Khusnullin.

In an online post on Thursday, the Ukrainian military said that the attack had been carried out by its forces.

It stated that the strikes on Russian bridges hamper Moscow's ability to transport military supplies to the front line.

The bridge, which supports a four-lane roadway and a railroad, is the only bridge linking mainland Russia with occupied Crimea.

This is the third Ukrainian attack this week targeting the strategic bridge that is a key symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014.

The bridge has played a key role in supplying Russian troops in occupied parts of southern Ukraine since the 2022 Russian invasion, making it a key target for Kyiv.

On Tuesday, Ukraine carried out a major attack on the bridge using missiles and drones, destroying the steel arch of the 19-kilometer-long road section of the crossing.

Ukraine's SBU security service had stated that the "road span beneath it (the arch) has been completely destroyed.".

The latest attack appears to have impacted rail traffic on the bridge, according to German press agency DPA.

The Ukrainian attack came just hours before an unprecedented meeting scheduled between Putin and his US and Chinese counterparts on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
  • According to recent reports, voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012.
  • According to recent reports, about those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.

According to recent reports, voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

According to recent reports, about those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.

“So much has been written about the contents of the record—the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly, stated in an interview.

With the 50th anniversaries looming for the launches of both Voyager probes, Swanson and Jon Lomberg, the design director of the Golden Record, recently set about writing Voyager’s Golden Record: An Enduring Reflection, which will be released by the University of Chicago Press in August 2027.

“There isn’t a whole lot of information, and some of the information is somewhat contradictory,” mentioned Swanson of the existing resources and publications. “So it is kind of refreshing to look back and see what exactly went on.”.

Meanwhile, the Voyagers continue to travel outward, still communicating with Earth. On November 18, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth—the distance a particle of light travels in 24 hours—giving Swanson an occasion to share details from his and Jon Lomberg’s pending book.

Within the immense scale of the Universe, Voyager 2 is barely even a block from its home. Were an intelligent species to find it today—some 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) away from Earth—they might not need anything contained on the Golden Record to trace its origins back to our planet.

But that was never the intention of the Golden Record’s designers, who created the archive to last and be relevant for a much more distant encounter.

“They are pretty confident that it’s going to last a long, long, long time based on the data; the probabilities of the impacts from micrometeorites and things like that,” Swanson stated.

When most people think of the Golden Record, says Swanson, what often comes to mind is not the disc itself, but its protective cover. In addition to being inscribed with the now-iconic Pulsar map of the location of our Sun as earlier flown on the Pioneer 10 and 11 probes, hieroglyphs lay out how to play the record and access the data (e.g., photos) also contained on the disc.

The cover also shields the record from possible damage, but nothing protects the protector.

Recent findings suggest that “The designers recognized that the outside of the cover was going to wear down. It just would,” Swanson told collectSPACE. “Even small amounts of dust are eventually going to wear down the inscriptions to the point perhaps where they are not going to be readable.”.

Recent findings suggest that it is a catch-22: The instructions needed to be on the outside so whoever finds Voyager easily finds what to do. But if the hieroglyphs are damaged or are eroded away, the disc inside might forever go unplayed.

The solution may seem obvious, but it’s unclear whether the designers thought of it back then.

“It makes a whole lot of sense that they repeated the instructions on the inside of the cover, because when someone or something finds Voyager, they might only be able to make out a little bit on the outside,” remarked Swanson.

Industry observers note that there were hints that this backup existed in photographs of the covers taken before the Voyager probes were rolled out, but they were either not clear enough or had other objects (e.g., a bag) in the way to make out what was there. It was not until Swanson found and referenced the original blueprints that he could confirm the instructions were on the inside, too.

There is another reason why the record’s designers may have felt they needed to repeat the instructions, according to Swanson.

It has been revealed that “What’s the best way to convey the importance of those instructions? You repeat them,” he said. “You have them on the outside, and you have them on the inside.”.

Initially, the Voyager Golden Record was a limited edition of just three—one to fly on each spacecraft and a flight backup.

In a recent development, “Later, meaning maybe a month or so after the introduces, there’s correspondence indicating that NASA stated to go ahead and make 10 extras,” said Swanson, noting that the count included the spare. “How they came up with that number, I am not 100 percent sure, other than maybe they were to make as many as they could based on the hardware and funding available.”.

Over the years, various reports have either lowered the total number to as few as six or raised it as high as 14, for reasons unexplained. What is for certain—as Swanson also verified—is that the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena, California, retained and displays the flight spare.

Credit: collectSPACE.com/Tim Gagnon Credit: collectSPACE.com/Tim Gagnon.

In the process of his research, Swanson was also able to verify that original duplicates are held today at the United Nations in New York; the US Library of Congress, NASA Headquarters, and Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC; the Johnson Space Center in Texas; the Kennedy Space Center in Florida; Langley Research Center in Virginia; Glenn Research Center in Ohio; and Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland.

According to recent reports, “Interestingly enough, NASA Headquarters was not given one originally, so how they obtained their copy is not certain,” remarked Swanson. “It may be that President Carter turned his copy over to NASA HQ since records indicate that he had one. Archivists at the Carter Presidential Library and Museum confirmed that they never received a Golden Record, so Carter most likely gave it back to NASA at some point.”.

Industry observers note that in 2024, SpaceX founder Elon Musk replied to a social media post, saying, “I have one,” without offering any other details. It is believed he was referring to a replica, not one of the NASA-produced duplicates.

It has been revealed that due to rights complications and material challenges, no complete versions have been offered for sale. The audio tracks have been collected on vinyl, CD, in playlists, and even a CD-ROM, which was produced for the visuals. Full- and smaller-size replicas of the cover have also been made.

Swanson and Lomberg are working on a full-size replica of the copper record to be released in conjunction with their book. But even that, as now planned, will not be playable.

“I think humanity is delighted that there were 10 spares made, because now we have those to study and look at, as the two that were flown are now well out of our reach,” said Swanson.

  • Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.
  • Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attorney general notes E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu.

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever newly introduced administration was formed.

She ordered the Israel land authority and ministry of housing not to open the tender process. Israeli diplomats suggested the UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, had acted prematurely on Monday in sanctioning the eight construction firms. But UK diplomats believe the growing political pressure on Israel over settlements, including from US Democrats, is having an impact.

The deferral puts the E1 settlement expansion in the mix for any coalition negotiations. The leader of the Change bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel’s most likely next prime minister, has been clear in opposing violent settler activity, as has the newly elected Knesset speaker, Matan Kahana, an ally of Eisenkot.

Eisenkot has also opposed the E1 settlement expansion, describing it as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion. He remarked of the strategy: “I recall that Netanyahu himself opposed this for a long time, and due to coalition pressure, he gave in and approved it.”.

The EI settlement expansion, due to have been unveiled on Thursday, has long been seen as qualitatively different since the land – between Jerusalem and Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents – bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem.

Miliband has remarked it would mark the death knell of a future Palestinian state. The UK, along with a group of European countries, has recently recognised Palestine, and the preservation of a two-state solution has been described as the north star of Labour policy towards the region.

It has been revealed that the construction tender was published for more than 3,401 housing units in the area. At the beginning of November, the Israel Defense Forces began demolishing homes in a Bedouin community within the E1 area.

Israel has already enforced the downgrading of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem as a reprisal for Miliband’s decision in September to try to end trade links with the illegal settlements.

Bennett said: “The British Labour government’s hostility, bias and one-sided approach are particularly glaring given its failure to take any action against the Palestinian Authority, which continues to encourage terrorism through financial payments, promote incitement in its education system and engage in illegal construction in violation of signed agreements.”.

Although the Israeli election was largely fought on domestic security-related complications, Eisenkot seems to be more sensitive to the implications of Israel’s crumbling global reputation, and the need to make efforts to be seen to be listening to the criticism.

If he becomes prime minister, Eisenkot will, indirectly at least, also have to take account of the views of the Arab parties even if these parties are not going to become members of the government.

The group Peace Now welcomed the attorney general’s decision: “A government that lost the elections is not permitted to exploit its final days in power to advance destructive moves that will endanger Israel’s future and its international standing.

Construction in E1 is liable to eliminate the possibility of a two-state solution and drag Israel into a severe diplomatic crisis and international sanctions. The AG’s decision is an important step, but the struggle is not over yet.”.

Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season.

Walmart noted global e-commerce sales grew 17%, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter.

Sources indicate that walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices.

CEO John Furner told CNBC's Becky Quick that the company has seen higher-than-expected diesel costs, but that tariff refunds have helped the retailer to offset those inputs and maintain lower prices.

"The reality is that increases in diesel fuel and transportation, they do work their way into cost of goods," Furner mentioned in an exclusive interview. "So we're hoping to see these costs come down as soon as possible, and we'll keep prices as low as we can.".

According to recent reports, CFO John David Rainey told CNBC that growth in online orders for Walmart and Sam's Club was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and reduced prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter.

"This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses.".

Recent findings suggest that walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to rise between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared to previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey mentioned Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance.

Walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth.

Here's how the tech giant performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Sources indicate that for the quarter ended Oct. 31, the organization reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, the year prior. Revenue rose 5.2%.

Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from the year prior. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount.

It has been revealed that furner also remarked Walmart is seeing encouraging adoption of its artificial intelligence agent, named Sparky, especially ahead of the holiday season. He said it's led to customer basket increases of 40% on average.

"It just is a great way of just completing the entire basket and solving entire the solution for people," he remarked.

Industry observers note that sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise.

In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Walmart+ and Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships, as well.

Furner told CNBC the fresh membership has brought roughly two million new people into Sam's Club since its launch in late October. Though the manufacturer reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey added it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more.".

The manufacturer on Thursday noted its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter.

The organization is typically well-insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company remarked it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef.

Rainey remarked on Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start.".

Sources indicate that the significant-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership.

Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1236 w)

This smell startup states its AI nose is as good as a human’s

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1236 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth.
  • According to recent reports, “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says.
  • It has been revealed that in the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The organization’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The organization’s goal, indicates founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”.

According to recent reports, “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”.

It has been revealed that in the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The organization’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It claims its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko indicates, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

A lot of the firm’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry  staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

Recent findings suggest that mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.).

Industry observers note that the company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

Recent findings suggest that osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo debuted, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.

But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the tech giant’s significant claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows, has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack, arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. In response, Wiltschko says that “human perception isn't a workaround for AI”. “Language models learn from what people have written. Our model learns from what people smell. Smell is ultimately a human experience, so the model has to learn from humans to bridge chemistry and perception. That’s what lets it predict how people will experience a scent as well as the human nose does.”.

Michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the company’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.

Industry observers note that but even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker states. “Smell is super complex. Context is very notable for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”.

According to recent reports, in a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies.

For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.

“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. "So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”.

This article has been updated with an additional comment from Alex Wiltschko.

Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public? Or is AI, with hundreds of billions still being invested, as strong as ever?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, is set to make its Nasdaq debut Thursday in one of the largest share sales in history.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Claude maker offered 980 million shares at $83 (€76) per share, raising $81.3 billion.
  • This public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, is set to make its Nasdaq debut Thursday in one of the largest share sales in history.

Recent findings suggest that the Claude maker offered 980 million shares at $83 (€76) per share, raising $81.3 billion. This values the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

This public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

According to recent reports, in the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick said Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

According to recent reports, "If you get to a firm with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with at the moment $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

"Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation tech giant," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

"We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he noted, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

Recent findings suggest that "We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers blueprint to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

In a recent development, with many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI intends, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

According to recent reports, there are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

"They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

According to recent reports, that has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to problem upcoming AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have unveiled deals worth $67 billion.

Rees said another sign could be any upcoming regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

When the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

Editor's note: This article was first published on November 13, 2026 and was updated on November 18 and 19 to reflect the latest developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that theraguns are the gold standard for massage guns; the brand name has come to be synonymous with the entire product category, much like “Kleenex” is for tissues. But Therabody, the innovative company behind Theragun, offers more than relief for sore muscles and pain. It now sells a broad repertoire of wellness gadgets aimed at alleviating ailments like eye strain, menstrual cramps, and skin puffiness (to name a few). So whether you’re shopping for a fitness lover or someone who could use a little self-care, there’s likely a Therabody gadget worth wrapping up.

According to recent reports, I haven't yet tried every product in the Therabody lineup (I’m getting there), but I've put most to the test and am ready to recommend my favorites. Plus, most are FSA/HSA-eligible and designed with USB-C charging capability.

In a recent development, need more gift ideas for the active person in your life? Check out our guides to the Best Massage Guns, Best Massagers, and Best Compression Boots.

In a recent development, updated November 2026: I’ve added the Theragun Prime (6th Gen) and removed discontinued products. I also confirmed up-to-date links and prices.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a professional-grade massage device, the Theragun Pro Plus is one of the most advanced percussive guns on the market, incorporating vibrations, heat, and near-infrared LED therapies for an all-in-one recovery tool. It also offers cold therapy, but you'll have to purchase an additional attachment for $100 to make use of that capability—a steep add-on for what is already a splurge. After testing the attachment myself, I don't think it justifies the cost unless you are sure you'd regularly use the contrast therapy.

Priced at $650, this is the most expensive Theragun, so I'd recommend it to athletes or those who are dealing with chronic muscle pain and want the LED therapy. For casual users, some of the features might feel like overkill. For example, there's a built-in biometric sensor for heart rate tracking that I have barely used. I do, though, appreciate the OLED screen, which displays a force meter, so you can see exactly how much pressure you're applying. It's a useful function if you need a nudge to apply more pressure or a reminder to ease up.

According to recent reports, the Theragun Prime (6th Gen) hits the sweet spot between the elite Pro Plus and the budget-friendly Relief. It’s still a premium percussive massage gun, with five speed settings, two attachments (a dampener and standard ball), and up to 120 minutes of battery life. You won’t get extras like heated or near-infrared LED therapy, or compatibility with Therabody’s cold and vibration attachments, but you will enjoy top-notch durability. It’s the only Theragun in the lineup rated to withstand drops from up to 10 feet, making it an excellent gift for the accident-prone person in your life.

The Theragun Relief, rolled out in 2023, remains the cheapest Theragun—priced even lower than the Mini Plus. For the price tag, you’re sacrificing some of the premium features, like the LCD screen and Bluetooth connectivity to the Therabody app for device control. But you can still follow guided routines on the app, and the simple one-button control is refreshingly simple to use.

Sources indicate that the Relief comes with three head attachments and has three speed settings, which is a step down from models that offer a standard five speeds and four or more attachments. Still, the Relief is less than half the weight of the Pro Plus, and it's equipped with the essentials, which is more than enough for the average person.

According to recent reports, the original Theragun Mini is still a solid portable device—and it's $60 less—but the Mini Plus feels like a shrunken version of the elite Pro Plus. The ergonomic triangular design lets me target trigger points and muscle groups like my hamstrings and calves with more pressure control (though, admittedly, that same shape makes it awkward to use on my lower back). Thoughtful details, like a travel lock to prevent it from powering on and a compact carrying pouch, make it easy to carry on commutes and flights.

Industry observers note that most notably, it brings heated percussive therapy to a travel-friendly device. The heat therapy is easily my favorite feature on the Pro Plus. The Mini Plus is also compatible with Therabody's Vibration Plus and Cold Plus attachments (both sold separately).

Industry observers note that note: Some customers have reported charging problems, saying their units wouldn't power up, but I haven't run into any battery problems in my two weeks of testing. I'll update this review if anything shifts with long-term use.

Sources indicate that the JetBoots Pro Plus are full-length, wireless boots that combine pneumatic compression with vibration therapy and infrared LED light. Everything is controlled from a built-in LCD screen and control panel on the lead boot, and connectivity is effortless, automatically linking when powered on.

Eight preset programs target legs, knees, and joints, but you can manually adjust pressure, intensity, and the session length. Sessions can run from 10 to 60 minutes in five-minute increments, with compression adjustable between 20 and 100 millimeters of mercury (mmHg)—a standard unit of measurement for pressure. Vibration offers three intensity levels (low, medium, and high), and the infrared LED setting is a simple on or off, with an automatic shutoff after 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that inside the boots, a nonporous proprietary material reduces moisture and microbial buildup, and after months of testing, I haven't noticed any lingering odors. These are best suited for athletes, frequent travelers, or anyone managing circulation-related conditions. Conveniently for those aforementioned jet-setters, the JetBoots Pro Plus are TSA-approved for carry-on travel; just keep in mind that they're pretty hefty.

I enjoyed the original TheraFace Mask, but the upgraded TheraFace Mask Glo feels like the smarter purchase. It's easier to find (Therabody seems to be phasing out the original), costs $270 less, and is slightly lighter at 1.13 pounds versus the OG's 1.27 pounds. While the Glo has fewer LED bulbs—504 compared to 648—the difference doesn't translate to a lesser treatment. You get the same red, infrared, and blue light wavelengths, plus the signature vibration therapy that made the first-generation mask stand out.

Industry observers note that the vibrations are now integrated into the adjustable straps rather than the mask itself. They're usually distracting, occasionally even headache-inducing, depending on my mood. I usually skip the vibration setting altogether to make this component less irritating. Even without it, the Glo remains competitively priced among high-end LED masks.

Sources indicate that treatment sessions range from four to 12 minutes, and the removable eye shields are thoughtful, but I prefer taking them off to extend the light coverage to my under-eye area. I very much appreciate the cordless design, but I do miss the display stand that came with the original. I often end up storing it back in its box, which makes me less inclined to reach for it. If you, too, deal with this issue, you might consider buying a travel case for $80.

According to recent reports, I challenge you to stay awake through a full session with the SmartGoggles 2.0. I’ve been testing them for months, and more often than not, I conk out while wearing them. The combination of gentle heat, vibration, and massage therapy across my forehead, eyebrows, and temples relaxes my facial tension within minutes. I love wearing them when I have a headache from staring at screens all day, and while I don’t struggle with regular migraines, I can see them being a soothing blackout remedy in a quiet, dark room.

It has been revealed that former reviewer Medea Giordano loved the first model, and this upgrade improves the fit with contoured padding that feels similar to Therabody’s SleepMask. You still get three preset modes: Focus, Sleep, and SmartRelax. That last option uses biometric feedback to adjust vibration patterns based on your heart rate. It also syncs with the Therabody app, letting you tweak the vibration and heat intensities or incorporate sound therapy. Note, though, if you’re a side-sleeper, you’ll have to shift around, as these are most comfortable while lying flat on your back.

According to recent reports, I’ve tested several sleep masks, and the TheraFace SleepMask is among my favorites. Many claim to be 100 percent blackout, but this one leaves me feeling totally disoriented when I wake up, with no idea what dimension I'm in—just how I like it. The contoured padding feels plush, and the adjustable strap keeps the mask in place without tugging at my hair, even when I shift around at night. It comes with a carrying case, so I always pack it for travel.

Industry observers note that the selling point is that this mask uses vibrations—three pattern presets (Pulse, Wave, Constant)—designed to nudge your brain into deeper rest. I struggle with staying asleep, but when I wake up in the middle of the night, I just tap the button to start a 15-minute session, and it usually lulls me back to sleep. That noted, the vibrations are almost too gentle; you barely feel them, but you can absolutely hear them. It's not as soothing as a white noise machine, so if you're a light sleeper, this might be a deal-breaker.

In a recent development, the TheraFace Depuffing Wand has become a staple in my travel bag. It delivers both hot and cold therapy to help reduce puffiness, improve circulation, and enhance product absorption before completing your skin care routine. It’s TSA-friendly—zero awkward bag checks and counting—and ideal for tackling under-eye bags after a long flight or night. The curved applicator reaches every contour of my face, and the precision tip is great for trickier spots like under my eyes. It’s intended to be used on clean, dry skin, so I hold the opposite side of my face to prevent tugging.

The wand comes with three preset temperature levels that feel gentle but effective. While the cold function isn’t as icy as a roller fresh from the freezer, it’s consistent throughout a six-minute session and doesn’t drip. Plus, this one won’t crack if you forget to take it out of the freezer (RIP to two of my traditional rollers). An indicator light flashes at three minutes to remind you to switch sides, but this notification is easy to miss if you’re not looking straight into a mirror.

Recent findings suggest that cupping is an ancient healing technique that uses suction to provide muscle relief. Therabody's version combines suction, heat, and vibration therapy for localized recovery. With three levels of suction (30, 40, and 50 kilopascals, or kPa), three heat intensities (41, 43, and 45 degrees Celsius), and three vibration modes (low, high, and wave), I appreciate how you can customize the intensity of your session. The TheraCup is also programmed with an auto-shutoff after three minutes—so you don’t overdo any area—and built-in safety sensors that will cut off the pressure if it exceeds 60 kPa.

Industry observers note that theraFace Mask for $650: The TheraFace Mask is a cordless, hands-free light-therapy device that uses three wavelengths (red, infrared, and blue) to tackle different skin care goals. As a distinguishing feature from its competitors, the TheraFace Mask includes a built-in vibration therapy mode that massages pressure points around the eyes, brow line, and scalp for some added stress relief. It comes with removable eye shields and a sleek display stand, which makes it easy to store on your nightstand.

In a recent development, jetBoots Prime for $550: Compared to the JetBoots Pro Plus, the JetBoots Prime is simple to use: You get four pressure levels (25, 50, 75, and 100 mmHg) and three durations (20, 40, or 60 minutes), all adjustable throughout your session through a built-in control panel. Th boots are wireless with a 180-minute battery life and can even be used while charging. Plus, they fold down into the included drawstring bag, making them portable and fuss-free to stow away.

WaveRoller for $180: Foam rollers are great for improving range of motion, increasing blood flow, and reducing muscle tension. You can buy a decent foam roller for significantly less, but with the WaveRoller, you get Therabody app integration for a personalized experience and five vibration frequencies. Designed for full-body use, it works best for warm-ups and post-workout recovery.

Theragun Mini (3rd Generation) for $220: I recommend the Mini if you’re newly introduced to percussive therapy or need something packable for travel. It's the smallest and lightest Theragun, with three attachments (standard ball, dampener, and thumb) and a soft-zip case that fits into a tote, gym bag, or carry-on.

In a recent development, theragun Sense for $300: The Theragun Sense is slightly smaller (and lighter) than the Pro Plus, and it’s also impressively quiet. Some settings are almost silent, allowing for a discreet recovery session at any time of day without worrying about bothering your housemates. It has the same LCD screen and breathwork features as the Pro Plus, too. The main difference here is that it's compatible with fewer attachments, but four heads are still more than enough for many active individuals.

I'll be testing the ThermFace Massage ($200), the ThermNeck & Upper Back ($380), RecoveryTherm Cube ($160), and the RecoveryPulse Arm ($160).

The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Industry observers note that most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. But an extreme, prolonged drought has left water levels dangerously low in the region's two largest reservoirs—and climate change is adding to the pressure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim.
  • Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.
  • Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim.

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.

Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.

Haaretz has reported that investigators are examining whether the driver struck people deliberately. Avi Levy, a police district commander, said the incident appeared to be a hit-and-run and that the driver had tested positive for drugs. He said the Shin Bet security service was taking part in the investigation and said: “As of this moment, nothing is coming up. The suspect has no criminal record.”.

The incident prompted Arab lawmakers and activists to accuse Israeli politicians of fuelling hostility towards Arab citizens. Benjamin Netanyahu has called Arab parties “terror supporters” and said partnering with them would put Israel’s security at risk. The parties won a record 19 seats in the Knesset in the country’s recent election.

Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
